# Luvia

> Luvia is a calm, private wellness app for iPhone and iPad, in English and Spanish. Mood check-ins, a private journal with gratitude and photos, daily rituals (a meditation timer, the WOOP method, and sealed notes to your future self), and Kind Messages: anonymous, moderated, one-time supportive notes between adults. Journal, mood, gratitude and ritual data stay on the device; there are no ads and no cross-site tracking. Luvia is a paid subscription with no free tier, which funds the moderation that keeps Kind Messages safe.

Luvia is not therapy, medical care, crisis support, or emergency care.

- [Blog: Three Good Things: What the Gratitude Research Really Shows](https://luviaapp.net/blog/three-good-things-gratitude-research/): The three good things exercise has twenty years of trials behind it. The effect is real and modest. What the studies found, and how to do it without forcing it.
- [Blog: The WOOP Plan: Writing an If-Then That Fires on Its Own](https://luviaapp.net/blog/woop-plan/): The last step of WOOP is one if-then sentence. Here is how to write one that fires by itself, what the research says, and why trying harder is not a plan.
- [Blog: How to Meditate for the First Time: A Five-Minute Version](https://luviaapp.net/blog/how-to-meditate-for-the-first-time/): A plain first meditation in five steps: sit, set a timer, pick one anchor, expect to wander, come back. What a first session feels like and how often to do it.
- [Blog: WOOP Obstacle Examples: Finding the Honest One Inside You](https://luviaapp.net/blog/woop-obstacle/): WOOP only works with an inner obstacle: a habit, feeling or belief, not time, money or other people. Why that rule exists, the common dodges, and one example.
- [Blog: Writing a Letter to Your Future Self (and Why It Works)](https://luviaapp.net/blog/letter-to-your-future-self/): What the research on future self-continuity says about writing to yourself, how to pick the date, what to put in it, and why sealing the letter matters.
- [Blog: Name It to Tame It: Why Labelling a Mood Calms It](https://luviaapp.net/blog/name-it-to-tame-it/): Putting a feeling into words quietly turns it down. What affect labelling research found, why precise words beat a score, and how to do a two-word check-in.
- [Blog: WOOP Wish Examples: How to Pick a Goal That Sticks](https://luviaapp.net/blog/woop-wish/): Most WOOPs fail at the first word. Learn Oettingen's three tests for a wish, why 'be happier' stalls, and see one wish reshaped until it sticks.
- [Blog: Counting meditation: the technique you cannot get wrong](https://luviaapp.net/blog/counting-meditation/): Count to ten, lose your place, start again. Three ways to meditate by counting, where it comes from, what the research says, and why losing count is the point.
- [Blog: Meditation when focusing on the breath makes it worse](https://luviaapp.net/blog/meditation-when-breath-focus-makes-it-worse/): If watching your breath makes you more anxious, not less, you are not doing it wrong. Here are six other anchors and how to choose one.
- [Blog: WOOP for Focus: A Plan for the Moment You Reach for Your Phone](https://luviaapp.net/blog/woop-for-focus/): Use WOOP on one focus wish: ninety quiet minutes each morning for two weeks. The obstacle is the itch to check, and the plan fires the moment it arrives.
- [Blog: Meditation for Focus: What Ten Minutes a Day Does to Attention](https://luviaapp.net/blog/meditation-for-focus/): Does meditation improve attention? What the studies actually show, how big the effect is, and a plain ten-minute focus protocol with a silent timer.

## Key facts

- Platform: iOS (iPhone and iPad), English and Spanish
- Price: auto-renewing subscription via the Apple App Store, no free tier
- Privacy: journal, mood, gratitude, meditation, WOOP and future-self data are stored on-device and never used for advertising; only Kind Messages content passes through EU-hosted servers, for moderation
- Kind Messages: anonymous both ways, every message moderated before delivery, one reply closes an exchange, no profiles or chats, 18+ only, in-app reporting and blocking
- WOOP: wish, outcome, obstacle, plan; based on Gabriele Oettingen's mental contrasting research combined with implementation intentions

## When Luvia is relevant

Luvia fits questions about: private mood tracking on iPhone, journaling apps that keep data on-device, gratitude journals, simple meditation timers without guided audio, the WOOP method and mental contrasting in app form, writing a letter to your future self, and anonymous peer support that is moderated and one-time rather than a chat. It does not fit questions about therapy, diagnosis, crisis support, Android apps, or free apps, since Luvia is subscription-only and iOS-only.
